chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'What is the most superior form of Hajj that people perform?' He said, 'Umrah in Rajab and a standalone Hajj in its year.'

I said, 'What follows this?' He said, 'Al-Mut'ah (Hajj al-Mut'ah).' I said, 'How does one perform it?' He said, 'The time comes and he enters into Ihram with Talbiyah for Hajj. When he arrives at Mecca, he performs Tawaf and Sa'i, and frees himself from Ihram from everything, while remaining resident, and he is not permitted to leave Mecca until he performs Hajj.'

I said, 'What follows this?' He said, 'Al-Qiran (Hajj al-Qiran), and Al-Qiran is that he drives the Hadi (sacrificial animal).' I said, 'What follows this?' He said, 'Standalone Umrah, and he goes wherever he wishes. If he stays in Mecca until the Hajj season, his Umrah is complete and his Hajj is incomplete (Meccan).'

I said, 'What follows this?' He said, 'What people do today: they perform standalone Hajj. When they arrive at Mecca and perform Tawaf around the House, they free themselves (from Ihram). When they make Talbiyah, they enter Ihram again, so they continue freeing and binding until they go out to Mina without Hajj and without Umrah.'

So it is not contradictory to what we mentioned, that Al-Mut'ah is the most superior of the types of Hajj in all cases, because what this report encompassed referred to one who performed Umrah in Rajab and stayed in Mecca until the time of Hajj and did not go out to perform Mut'ah, so for him there is only Al-Ifrad.

As for one who went out to his homeland, then returned at the time of Hajj, or stayed in Mecca then went out to some of the Miqat and entered Ihram with Al-Mut'ah for Hajj, he is more superior according to what we presented, and that which indicates this is what he narrated.

key_terms.الْإِفْرَادُ: Hajj al-Ifrad, where one performs Umrah first, exits Ihram, then re-enters Ihram specifically for Hajj.
key_terms.الْقِرَانُ: Hajj al-Qiran, where Umrah and Hajj are combined in a single Ihram.
key_terms.الْمُتْعَةُ: Hajj al-Mut'ah (Hajj of Temporal Connection), a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately with a break in between.
key_terms.الْهَدْيَ: The sacrificial animal brought by the pilgrim.
key_terms.مِنًى: Minah, a plain near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj.
key_terms.يَحَلُّ: To exit the state of Ihram after completing the rituals of Umrah.
key_terms.يُلَبِّي: To recite the Talbiyah (the invocation of entering Ihram).

ai.seo_question: What is the most superior type of Hajj and how is it performed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a nuanced hierarchy of Hajj types, with Imam al-Baqir (AS) declaring Al-Mut'ah as the most superior due to its combination of Umrah and Hajj. The text clarifies that while Ifrad is the default for those performing Umrah in Rajab and staying in Mecca, Mut'ah is preferred for those who explicitly enter Ihram for it from their Miqat, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the distinct ritual sequence of Umrah followed by Hajj.
